sonnet.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess the wording of a line, "words of ___ and truth." Nothing earlier in Stop 2 sets up Esther 9:30, so the baker can only guess. Peace, warning and judgment are all equally plausible.
sonnet.rule: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

sonnet.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess the wording of a line, "times of ___ and lamentation." Verse 31 was never set up on a story card, so the baker cannot reason out "fasting" from anything they have seen.
sonnet.rule: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

sonnet.problem: This joke repeats the idea and punchline shape of Stop 1 card 3, "I had YEARS of rest in a junk drawer" and "I spent YEARS back there." It is the same joke idea twice in one lesson, and it is not a callback that adds anything new.
sonnet.rule: Each joke idea, comparison and punchline shape is used once per lesson. A callback is the one exception, and it adds something new.
